surfaces.part: ice crack decal (jagged blue line with pale highlight, lying flat)

answer.evidence: The silhouette is a thin jagged zig-zag line, 1-2 px thick, with a dark blue row (#24548c) over a pale highlight row (#cff4f8). It spans rows 4-13 with no volume, no front face and no standing structure. The column scans show only 2-row dark/light pairs. It is a flat floor decal seen from above, which matches the flat kind. It has no front face, so it reads as top-down.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a thin light-blue crack line, drawn in only 3 colours, on a flat dark slate background. It is not a 4x3-tile ground patch and has no ramp of shading steps, just a line and one or two tints. The measured visible tones per tile are 0 because the piece is smaller than a tile, so I judged by eye. The reference grass shows about 3 visible tones with tufts and speckle, and the paving shows about 7 tones with stones shaded one by one. Next to them the candidate's ground is a flat, grainless fill with no dots, tufts or variation, so it looks much thinner and flatter. There is no outline, so no dark material-tone edging is present. The crack itself is a sparse object, so I did not fail it on sparseness alone. I fail it because the surrounding surface has no texture or shading comparable to the references.

surfaces.part: ice crack decal (thin jagged line lying on ground)

Silhouette widths peak at 20 px on row 8 and narrow to 1 px, which is a crack outline, not a body. It reads as a flat top-down decal, which fits the kind flat.
